reasoning:
Since this is round one, there are no prior edits to reconcile with. I'm drafting the JSON edits now, refining the placed-cube rule to clarify the format and ensure released cubes are counted regardless of gripper position or later same-color detections, plus starting on the memory policy prompts.

Now I'm working through the subgoals: pinning down the holding rule to reference the last listed frame and partly closed fingers, establishing color priority based on the last placed entry or remaining need, defining stable candidate criteria that avoid flickering detections, and setting tie-break logic to prefer the nearest bin over nearest gripper fallback, quoting the exact rule text for each as I finalize the JSON.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: Rule 1 (holding): If the scene at this decision step shows a cube 'held in the gripper', choose B: put it into the bin. This holds whatever `placed` contains.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: Rule 1 (holding): The scene at this decision step is the LAST listed observed step; check that frame first, before any earlier execution frame. If any object line in that last frame ends in 'is held in the gripper', or the fingers there are partly closed (about 46% or less open), choose B: put it into the bin, before any other rule is considered. This holds whatever `placed` contains and however many cubes lie on the table.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: Where two colors are still needed, take the one with the larger remaining count (ties: either).
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: Color choice: if the last entry of `placed` is a color whose required count is not yet met, pick that color again (one color is finished before the other is started); otherwise, including when `placed` is empty, pick any color that still has fewer entries than required.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: Prefer a cube of that color that was already visible at the same place in the earlier execution steps of this decision step (or, at step #1, simply any cube of that color), and avoid detections that flicker in and out or that lie on top of the bin's position; cubes of other colors are distractors and are never picked.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: A candidate is a cube of the needed color reported as a table cube (not held) at the same coordinates, within about 2 px, in every execution frame of this decision step including the first one (at step #1, with no execution frames, any cube of that color in the scene is a candidate). A detection that first appears during the step, that sits where the held cube was last reported, that is reported within about 25 px of the bin's center, or whose position moves between frames is not a candidate while any stable one exists. Among several stable candidates, prefer the one nearest the bin's reported center without overlapping it. The point is that candidate's center as reported in the last frame. Cubes of other colors are distractors and are never picked.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: otherwise choose A pointing at the cube of a needed color nearest the gripper, and if none is visible at all, choose A pointing at any visible cube.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: otherwise choose A pointing at the stable cube of a needed color nearest the bin (not overlapping it), and if none is visible at all, choose A pointing at any visible cube not overlapping the bin.

edits.modify_from: Start with an empty list when the memory is empty.
edits.modify_to: When the carried-in memory is empty, write the literal [] as this step's value. The value is always a JSON array of double-quoted strings, exactly like the carried-in value and the example: ["green", "green"], never ['green', 'green'] and never a blank.

edits.modify_from: then the robot has just released a cube into the bin, so append that held cube's color once.
edits.modify_to: then the robot has just released a cube into the bin, so append that held cube's color once. The oracle always runs the put-into-bin subgoal to completion, so this held-then-released pattern is always a successful placement: append whatever the gripper position at release (it is often 30-50 px from the bin's reported center) and whatever cubes appear, move or vanish on the table in the same frames. e.g. carried-in ["red"] becomes ["red", "red"].
The value is always written as a JSON array of double-quoted color strings; at step #1 it is the literal [] (an explicit empty array, never a blank).

edits.modify_from: Count released cubes even if a cube of that color later appears somewhere on the table, since the bin is opaque and detections near it are unreliable.
edits.modify_to: That held-then-released event is always one completed bin placement: count it regardless of where the gripper was reported when the fingers opened (often 30-50 px from the bin's reported center) and regardless of any same-color cube detection appearing on the table at or near the release point in the same frames, since the bin is opaque and detections near it are unreliable. Example sequence over an episode: [] -> [] -> ["green"] -> ["green"] -> ["green", "green"].

revision.refused: The report's request for one exact geometric rule reproducing every recorded choice among same-color cubes stays out: the report itself finds that nearest-bin holds only about three quarters of the time and every other candidate (largest y, image center, nearest gripper) fails more often, so nearest-bin is committed as a preference and no further tie-break is added. No rule for which color to start with when `placed` is empty is committed, since the recorded first picks follow neither the named order nor the required counts; the instruction says any needed color is acceptable there. The suggestion that a first-step point was a composite of several detections stays out, as the recorded point lies within 2 px of a listed cube. A distance threshold alone for 'on the bin' is not made the primary test; the stability rule covers the ghost at the release point, and the 25 px exclusion is kept only as a secondary filter.
